title: Allocation vs latency budgeting — Azimuth Consulting intake
summary: Discovery to map Azimuth's budget-constrained production plan: evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private, acceptable latency SLOs, and cost levers (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization). Agreement to run a 2-week pilot benchmark with per-token vs reserved pricing scenarios.
questions: What token mix (prompt vs completion) do you expect?
Are there compliance constraints (data residency, SOC2)?
What's your monthly budget envelope for inference?
Do you need model weights on-prem or only inference inside VPC?
action_items: Samir: Send per-token pricing spreadsheet and a reserved capacity worksheet by 2026-07-21
Lisa: Share sample benchmark harness and instructions for synthetic load tests by 2026-07-22
Tom: Provide token distribution examples (avg prompt, avg completion, % streaming) by 2026-07-23
Ethan: Confirm network egress and VPC peering constraints and any firewall rules by 2026-07-24
next_steps: Redwood to provision pilot: 2-week hosted benchmark with 3 model variants (base, quantized, trimmed)
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) week of 2026-07-27 to tune batching and KV policies
Customer to share eval dataset and sample prompts for quality check
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lisa (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE brief join), Tom (Azimuth Head of ML), Maria (CTO), Ethan (Cloud Infra), Nora (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to map budget and latency trade-offs. Pilot agreed.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — I'm Samir, AE, Lisa's our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Tom (Azimuth): Good, thanks. we've been trying to reconcile latency targets with a pretty tight monthly budget so hoping to understand your hosted/dedicated/private options.
[00:18] Maria (CTO): yeah, to add, we have two main product lanes: interactive assistant (low latency, 1-2s target) and nightly batch re-ranking (throughput focused).
[00:29] Lisa (Redwood SE): makes sense. can you share the budget envelope roughly? it helps orient — per month or pilot?
[00:35] Tom: for pilot maybe $10k-$20k; long-term we're looking at a hard cap of about $50k/mo for inference across both products.
[00:44] Ethan (Infra): and security wise we need SOC2 compliance, SSO (SAML), and optional VPC/private deployment for PII flows. KMS for key management is non-negotiable.
[00:56] Samir: perfect, that's the kind of constraints we usually design for. quick overview: Redwood hosted gives fastest time to value with per-token pricing; Dedicated is reserved capacity GPU pools with committed throughput; Private is our VPC/on-prem offering for stricter residency and key control.
[01:14] Nora (Product): can you say more about the per-token math — especially how batching and caching affect cost?
[01:20] Lisa: yeah, so per-token cost is a function of total tokens rendered plus the efficiency gains from batching and prefix/KV caching. if you have many repeated prompts or high prefix reuse — KV cache can reduce compute per token because we don't recompute earlier layers. similarly batching reduces overhead — but the tradeoff is latency.
[01:38] Ethan: so is batching something we control client-side or does Redwood auto-batch?
[01:43] Lisa: Redwood runtime does continuous batching and we expose knobs — target latency SLO, batch window, and we can suggest policies. in hosted mode we have sane defaults and can tune; with Dedicated you can push batching more aggressively because you have predictable GPUs.
[01:58] Tom: curious about tail latency. for interactive assistant we need 95th < 200ms ideally. can you hit that on hosted?
[02:05] Lisa: depends on model and sequence length. for smaller models and short completions, hosted with optimized kernels can get into that range. but in many enterprise cases teams choose Dedicated to guarantee tail SLOs since dedicated pools reduce cold jitter and contention.
[02:20] Maria: and quantization? we want to reduce cost but can't degrade quality. what's the guidance?
[02:25] Lisa: we recommend model-specific quantization profiles. some models quantize well and keep quality; others need evals. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization per workload and we tie regressions to prompt sets. we'll run N examples during pilot to measure quality delta.
[02:38] Tom: what's the jump in unit price between hosted per-token vs reserved capacity? ballpark.
[02:42] Samir: ballpark hosted per-token is higher for bursty usage but no commitment. reserved (Dedicated) gets you lower unit cost when you commit to monthly capacity — think 20–50% lower unit cost depending on commitment and batching. exact depends on model and token mix. we'll send a worked example.
[03:01] Ethan: network-wise for Private we need to keep weights on our subnet and use our KMS. is that supported?
[03:07] Ravi (brief): yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS and you can run inference in a VPC or on-prem package. there are options to keep model blobs private or have Redwood manage them with strict attestations.
[03:18] Nora: any compliance caveats? do you have SOC2 and audit logs?
[03:21] Samir: we have SOC2 and we surface audit logs, RBAC, SSO. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:30] Tom: can you walk through an example calculation? say our interactive path average prompt 80 tokens, completion 40 tokens, 10M requests/month.
[03:38] Lisa: okay, quick mental math — that's ~1.2B tokens/month (10M*(80+40)=1.2B). with hosted per-token at, say, $0.00003 per token (example), that would be about $36k. but batching and KV cache can reduce effective tokens occasionally — if you have prefix reuse, cost could drop 10-30%. Dedicated with reservation and aggressive batching could bring it under your $50k cap comfortably and leave room for batch reranks.
[04:05] Tom: that per-token number sounds optimistic — is that for small models?
[04:09] Lisa: yes it's model dependent — for a 13B-like model unquantized the per-token goes up. we'll include model-specific sample pricing in the spreadsheet.
[04:18] Ethan: for batch reranking — that's throughput priority — any suggestions to minimize cost?
[04:22] Lisa: run batch on Dedicated or Private with larger batch windows; use quantized model variant and disable streaming; also use prefix/KV so repeated contexts are cached. you can schedule during off-peak to exploit reserved capacity.
[04:36] Maria: how do fallbacks work if capacity is constrained? we want graceful degradation.
[04:41] Samir: we have smart routing: by policy you can fallback to cheaper model variants or different region or capacity tier. Redwood can do A/B style rollouts or automatic fallback to avoid outages.
[04:52] Tom: what's the pilot look like? we want concrete numbers.
[04:56] Samir: propose a two-week pilot: Redwood runs a hosted benchmark with 3 model profiles (full, quantized, trimmed) using your sample prompts. we produce per-token cost estimates, latency distributions (p50, p95, p99), and guidance for Dedicated sizing to meet SLOs.
[05:12] Nora: will you need access to production data?
[05:15] Lisa: ideally you provide a sanitized sample set; if you need, we can run synthetic traffic. for sensitive flows we can do Private or VPC test where data doesn't leave your network.
[05:26] Ethan: any limits to concurrency for hosted? we need to understand throttles.
[05:29] Lisa: hosted has rate limits by default but can be relaxed for pilots; Dedicated is recommended for sustained concurrency and predictable throughput.
[05:38] Tom: one last thing — do you support streaming tokens and function calling? we rely on streaming for UX.
[05:44] Samir: yes hosted supports streaming and function/tool calling. there's some cost nuance when streaming since you may emit tokens earlier but overall batching still helps server-side.
[05:54] Maria: OK. on the purchasing side, if we liked Dedicated, what's the lead time?
[05:58] Samir: typically 2–4 weeks to stand up a dedicated pool depending on size and legal, sometimes faster with commit. Private on-prem is longer — depends on infra.
[06:07] Tom: are there hidden costs — e.g., egress, storage for KV caches, log retention?
[06:12] Lisa: egress depends on your cloud and region, storage for KV/prefix cache is modest and included in Dedicated; extended observability retention is an add-on. we'll call those out in the pricing doc.
[06:22] Ethan: can we get a worked example where we compare: 1) hosted per-token, 2) small Dedicated reserved (50% commit), 3) Private with on-prem weights — so we can present to finance?
[06:33] Samir: absolutely. that's the core of the pilot deliverable. we'll include the break-even and sensitivity to batching and prefix reuse.
[06:40] Nora: what are decision criteria we should prepare?
[06:43] Lisa: typically latency SLOs (p95), monthly spend, security/residency needs, and operational overhead. if you value low ops and speed, hosted wins. if cost predictability and SLO guarantees matter — Dedicated. if residency/KMS/runtime control is required — Private.
[06:58] Tom: any concerns about model drift or monitoring?
[07:02] Lisa: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets so you get regression alerts. we can integrate with your eval pipelines.
[07:10] Samir: quick recap and next steps?
[07:13] Tom: yes please.
[07:15] Samir: action items: Samir will send pricing spreadsheet and example math, Lisa will send benchmark harness and instructions, customer to send sample prompts and token distribution. agreed pilot scope — 2 weeks hosted benchmark with 3 model variants.
[07:29] Maria: that timeline works. we'll try to get the samples to you by Friday.
[07:33] Ethan: and I'll check with infra about firewall/VPC peering constraints.
[07:36] Nora: schedule the SE deep-dive for the week of 2026-07-27, please.
[07:40] Samir: done — we'll send calendar invites after the call.
[07:44] Tom: thanks everyone. this was useful — definitely more clarity on tradeoffs.
[07:48] Samir: thanks all, talk soon.

Notes: Transcript has small mis-transcriptions and timestamps roughly every 30–90s. Some product names may be written as Redwood Dedicated/Private or shorthand. Pilot deliverable will include per-token worked examples and p95/p99 latency curves.
